title: A Swollen Laptop Battery: What to Do Before the Lid Is Forced Shut
label: Battery
lead: The trackpad sits higher than it did last month, or the lid no longer closes flat. That rise is the pack pushing up from inside.
signs: The palm rest is no longer flat. A sweet or sharp smell sits near the keyboard. The lid leaves a gap when you try to shut it.
avoid: Do not poke the swelling, do not stack books on the lid, and do not keep charging the machine overnight.
bench: The pack is disconnected before anything else is tested. A swollen pack is replaced. The bay and the connector are checked so the new pack sits flat.
detail: A swollen cell has made gas. The case is holding that pressure. Leaving it on charge does not settle the cell back down. The job is a new pack the machine accepts, named before it is ordered.
scene: a laptop trackpad pushed upward by a swollen battery on a blue repair mat

title: A Laptop Hinge That Will Not Hold the Screen
label: Repairs
lead: The screen falls shut when you let go, or the lid only opens on one side. The hinge, not the picture, is the fault.
signs: One corner of the lid lifts while the other stays down. A crack has started in the plastic beside the hinge. The screen wobbles when the desk is bumped.
avoid: Do not open and shut the lid to work it loose. That finishes the broken screw bosses.
bench: The hinge and the posts it screws into are looked at together. A new hinge is fitted only when the posts can still hold it. If the posts are gone, the cover that carries them is part of the quote.
detail: A hinge that still turns but will not stay is not a software setting. Tightening the bezel screws from the outside rarely reaches the broken post. The bench opens the lid end and says which piece is spent.
scene: a laptop hinge with a cracked plastic cover on a repair bench

title: A Laptop Screen That Flickers When the Lid Moves
label: Screen
lead: The picture is steady on a desk and breaks into flicker when you change the angle of the lid. That points at the cable or the hinge path, not at a setting.
signs: The flicker follows the lid. An external screen stays steady while the laptop glass does not. A light tap near the hinge changes the picture.
avoid: Do not keep working with the lid at the one angle that still holds a picture. The cable is already tired.
bench: The cable that runs through the hinge is tested by moving the lid on the bench. A new panel is not ordered until the cable has been ruled out.
detail: A panel fault usually stays wrong at every angle. A cable fault changes when the lid moves. Naming which one it is keeps the quote to the part that failed.
scene: a laptop screen flickering as the lid is held at an angle on a workbench

title: Sound, a Fan, and a Black Laptop Screen
label: Screen
lead: You hear the startup sound, or the fan, and the glass stays black. The machine may be awake behind a dark panel, or it may never be drawing a picture at all.
signs: A torch at a low angle shows a faint desktop. An external screen shows a picture the laptop glass does not. Caps lock answers, and the glass does not.
avoid: Do not keep the brightness keys as the whole test. A dead backlight does not answer them.
bench: Backlight, cable, and panel are separated on the bench. A board fault is named only when those three are not the cause.
detail: A faint image in a torch beam means the panel is drawing and the light behind it is not. A completely blank glass, with a good picture on an external screen, is a different part. The quote follows that split.
scene: a dark laptop screen with a small torch showing a faint desktop

title: Water on a Laptop Keyboard: The First Hour
label: Keyboard
lead: A glass went over. The keys are wet, or the laptop shut itself off. What you do before you reach the counter decides how far the water travels.
signs: The machine died as the water landed. Some keys work and some do not. A damp patch is spreading under the palm rest.
avoid: Do not turn it back on to see if it survived, and do not use a hair dryer on hot. Do not shake it hard.
bench: The pack is disconnected. The wet area is dried and checked for corrosion. Keys are replaced when they no longer make contact. A board is named only if the spill reached it.
detail: Power on a wet board is what turns a spill into a burnt track. Switching it off, unplugging the charger, and carrying it in is the useful part of the first hour.
scene: a wet laptop keyboard with a tipped glass beside it on a wooden desk

title: Laptop Keys That Stick or Type the Wrong Letter
label: Keyboard
lead: One key needs a hard press. Another types twice. A third does nothing. Dirt, a torn membrane, and a spilled drink do not share a fix.
signs: Crumbs sit in the gaps. A letter repeats on its own. The same word always drops one character.
avoid: Do not pry every cap off with a knife. The scissor under a key bends, and then the cap will not sit.
bench: The bench says whether a clean will restore the contact or whether the keyboard has to be replaced. A replacement is named before it is ordered, because some machines need the whole top case.
detail: A single dead key after a spill is often the membrane, not one loose cap. Putting the cap back on a dead switch does not restore the letter.
scene: loose laptop keycaps and a small brush on a blue repair mat

title: A Laptop That Charges Only When the Plug Is Held
label: Repairs
lead: The charge light comes on when you push the plug upward, and it goes out when you let go. The socket, the plug, or the jack inside has worn.
signs: The light flickers as the cable moves. The percentage falls even though the brick is warm. A different angle of the plug is the only way it charges.
avoid: Do not wedge the plug with a pencil and leave it overnight. The worn contact will spark.
bench: The jack and the charger are tested apart. A loose jack is resoldered or replaced. A tired plug is replaced without opening the board, when the board side is still sound.
detail: Both sides can be worn at once. The counter checks the brick on another machine, then the socket on this one, and the quote names the side that failed.
scene: a loose laptop charging plug held at an angle to make the light come on

title: A Laptop That Switches Off When It Gets Hot
label: Repairs
lead: The work is fine for twenty minutes. Then the fan roars and the machine goes black. Heat, not a dead pack, is the usual reason for that pattern.
signs: It dies on a cushion and survives on a table. The palm rest is too hot to rest on. It returns only after it has cooled.
avoid: Do not keep starting it the moment it dies. Let it cool, and do not open the fan yourself.
bench: The fan, the heat sink, and the paste are the job when shutdown follows heat. A pack test is added only if the machine also dies while it is cool.
detail: Dust packed in the fins makes the fan loud and the chip hot. Cleaning the vent from outside does not clear the fins. That is bench work.
scene: a dusty laptop fan and heatsink removed on a repair bench

title: A Laptop Fan That Never Goes Quiet
label: Repairs
lead: A fan that runs hard on the desktop, with nothing open, is telling you the heat is not leaving or the fan bearing is done.
signs: A rattle starts as it spins up. The noise stays after you close every program. The air from the vent is weak even though the sound is loud.
avoid: Do not oil the fan through the vent. Do not block the vent to muffle it.
bench: The fan is spun on the bench and the fins are checked. A bearing that rattles is a new fan. A clean fan that still cannot hold temperature needs the paste and the sink looked at.
detail: A new fan does not fix a sink that is clogged. The quote should say whether you are buying a fan, a clean, or both.
scene: an open laptop base with the cooling fan exposed on a blue mat

title: Laptop Wi-Fi That Drops in the Same Room
label: Repairs
lead: The phone stays on the network and the laptop falls off. The fault can be the card, the antenna in the lid, or a setting that forgets the network after sleep.
signs: It drops when the lid moves. Other devices in the room stay online. It reconnects only after a restart.
avoid: Do not keep forgetting the network and typing the password as the only repair. If the antenna wire is off, that will not hold.
bench: The wireless card and the antenna leads are checked. A lead that has pulled off the card is reseated. A dead card is replaced with one the machine accepts.
detail: An antenna that runs up the hinge can fail the same way a screen cable does, when the lid has been opened for years. The bench looks there before it calls the router the cause.
scene: tiny antenna wires beside a laptop wireless card on a repair bench

title: A Laptop With No Sound From the Speakers
label: Repairs
lead: The volume is up, the mute mark is off, and a video still plays in silence. Headphones may work when the speakers do not, which splits the fault in two.
signs: Headphones play and the speakers do not. Nothing plays, not even headphones. The sound returns for a minute after a restart and then goes.
avoid: Do not install a stack of sound drivers from a search page. One wrong package can be the next fault.
bench: Speaker, codec, and jack are separated. A speaker that is physically open or unplugged is a part. A codec that failed after a fall can be the board.
detail: If headphones are also silent, the speakers are not the first part to buy. The counter says which side is dead before a speaker pair is ordered.
scene: a small laptop speaker removed beside an open laptop chassis

title: A Touchpad That Clicks but Will Not Move the Pointer
label: Repairs
lead: The click is still there. The pointer does not move, or it jumps to a corner and stays. A USB mouse may work the whole time.
signs: A mouse works and the pad does not. The pointer drifts while your palms rest. The pad works until Windows finishes starting.
avoid: Do not peel the pad off. On many machines it is part of the top case.
bench: The cable under the pad and the pad itself are checked. A replacement is quoted only when the cable is sound and the pad is not. Palm rejection is a setting, and the bench says when it is only that.
detail: A pointer that jumps when you type is often the palm, not a dead pad. A pointer that never moves, while a mouse does, is the pad or its cable.
scene: a laptop touchpad cable lifted during a repair on a blue mat

title: USB Ports That No Longer See a Mouse or a Drive
label: Repairs
lead: One port is dead and the other still works, or every port has gone quiet. A dead port is not always a dead board.
signs: A lamp on a USB stick never lights in one socket. The same stick works in the other socket. Every socket died after a short at the plug.
avoid: Do not force a bent plug back in to test it again. That takes the pins with it.
bench: The port is inspected for bent pins and for a short. A single port can be replaced. When the controller behind all of them has failed, the quote says board, not socket.
detail: One working port means the controller is still alive. That is the useful test before anyone talks about a board.
scene: a close view of a damaged laptop USB port with a bent metal tongue

title: A Laptop That Will Not Show a Picture on Another Screen
label: Screen
lead: The television stays on no signal and the laptop screen is fine. The cable, the port, and the graphics output are three different jobs.
signs: Another cable still fails. The laptop sees the television and shows a black picture. The port is loose in the case.
avoid: Do not buy a third cable until one known-good cable has been tried on another machine.
bench: The port is checked for bent pins and a cracked solder joint. A graphics fault is named only when a known-good cable and a known-good screen still stay dark.
detail: A port that wobbles has often cracked its joints. Resoldering that port is a smaller job than a board, and the counter says which one it is after the look.
scene: an HDMI cable plugged into the side of a laptop on a desk

title: A Laptop That Shows a Blue Screen and Restarts
label: Repairs
lead: A blue screen once, after a new program, is not the same as a blue screen every morning on the way to the desktop.
signs: It names a file and then restarts. It appears only when the machine is hot. It appears before you can sign in.
avoid: Do not keep reinstalling Windows as the first move if your files are only on that disk.
bench: Memory, disk, and heat are checked before a clean install is offered. A clean install is the job when the system itself is corrupt and the disk is sound. The files are talked about before that install starts.
detail: A blue screen that only happens when the palm rest is hot belongs with the fan, not with a new copy of Windows. The pattern matters more than the stop code you half remember.
scene: a laptop on a desk showing a blue error screen, no readable text

title: A Laptop That Became Slow Right After an Update
label: Repairs
lead: It was usable on Friday and heavy on Monday, and an update sat in between. The update may be the cause, or it may have exposed a disk that was already failing.
signs: The desktop arrives late only since the update. The disk light stays on. A rollback is offered and you have not taken it.
avoid: Do not start a second large update on a machine that is already stalling.
bench: The disk health and the startup programs are looked at. A failing disk is not fixed by removing the update. A healthy disk with a bad update can be rolled back or repaired without a new part.
detail: Say whether the slowness is the whole machine or one new program. That sentence changes the job.
scene: a laptop installing an update with a progress circle, no readable text

title: Pop-up Windows That Will Not Leave the Laptop Screen
label: Repairs
lead: A window says the laptop is infected, or that files are locked, and it asks to be paid. That window is the problem, not a bill from this shop.
signs: The browser opens a page you did not ask for. A voice from the speakers tells you to call a number. New icons appeared that you did not install.
avoid: Do not call the number on the window, and do not pay it. Do not give it remote control.
bench: The unwanted software is removed and the startup list is cleaned. A disk is checked only if the machine is also clicking or losing files. The quote names a clean, not a magic promise.
detail: A locked-file window is a common lie. The files are usually still there. The counter says what it actually found before any paid work.
scene: a laptop screen full of warning popups, text deliberately unreadable

title: A Windows Password You Can No Longer Type
label: Repairs
lead: The password that worked last month does not work now. Resetting it and wiping the account are not the same job, and one of them costs you the files inside that account.
signs: The hint is wrong. Another account on the same laptop still opens. You are not sure which email was used to create it.
avoid: Do not keep guessing until the machine locks you out for a long wait, and do not hand the laptop to a stranger who offers to remove the password with no talk of your files.
bench: The counter says whether a reset can keep the files or whether the only honest path is a new account and a loss of the old profile. Nothing here promises every password can be read back.
detail: A Microsoft account and a local account do not reset the same way. Bring the email you think you used. That detail changes the first step.
scene: a laptop sign-in screen with a blank password box, no readable text

title: A BitLocker Screen Asking for a Recovery Key
label: Repairs
lead: A blue screen asks for a long recovery key before the desktop. The key is not stored in the laptop. It was saved to an account or printed when encryption was turned on.
signs: It appeared after a BIOS update or a board change. You never turned encryption on yourself. The key is in an old email you cannot open without this laptop.
avoid: Do not pay a website that claims it will generate the key. Do not clear the disk until you have decided the files can go.
bench: The shop can reinstall Windows when you accept that the encrypted files go with the old system. It cannot invent a key that was never saved. The counter says that before any work.
detail: Look in the Microsoft account that was on the machine, from a phone, before you walk in. If the key is there, you may not need a repair at all.
scene: a laptop recovery key prompt, digits blurred and unreadable

title: A Hard Disk That Clicks When the Laptop Starts
label: Storage
lead: A click, then a pause, then another click, and the desktop is late or missing. That sound is the disk failing to read.
signs: The click is new. Files have started to vanish. The machine boots only on the third try.
avoid: Do not keep restarting it to catch a good boot, and do not save new work onto that disk.
bench: The disk is tested once, not hammered. If the files matter, that is said before the cover comes off. A new SSD or disk is the repair when the old one will not hold. Nothing here promises every file comes back.
detail: A clicking disk gets worse each time it is powered. Switch it off and carry it. A longer note on the new disk is in the SSD article on this site.
scene: a laptop hard disk on a blue mat next to an open laptop bay

title: An SSD the Laptop No Longer Sees
label: Storage
lead: The drive was there last week. Now the firmware says there is no disk, or Windows asks where to install.
signs: It disappeared after a bump. It disappears when the palm rest is pressed. A second SSD in a USB case is seen, and the internal one is not.
avoid: Do not initialise the disk if you still want the files on it. Initialising is a wipe.
bench: The socket, the drive, and the file system are separated. A loose drive is reseated. A dead drive is replaced, and the files are discussed first. A drive that is seen and unreadable is not the same quote as a drive that is absent.
detail: Pressing the palm rest and watching the drive vanish means a contact, not a format. The bench looks at that before it talks about a new disk.
scene: an M.2 SSD lifted from a laptop slot on a repair bench

title: A Disk So Full the Laptop Can Barely Open a File
label: Storage
lead: The warning says the disk is full. The desktop is slow, updates fail, and a new photo will not save. Space and a dying disk can look the same until someone measures.
signs: The drive is above the warning line. Deleting one folder helps for a day. The machine is slow even after a large delete.
avoid: Do not delete a folder you do not recognise just because it is large. Some of those folders are Windows.
bench: The bench says how much is files and how much is a disk that can no longer be trusted. A clean of unwanted programs is one job. A larger SSD is another. They are quoted apart.
detail: Freeing a little space does not repair a clicking disk. If you hear a click, stop deleting and bring it in.
scene: a laptop storage warning on screen with the words out of focus

title: Signs a Laptop Needs More Memory, Not a New Machine
label: Repairs
lead: One program is fine. Four programs, and the fan starts and the window goes white. That pattern is often memory that is too short for the work.
signs: A browser with many tabs is the moment it stalls. The same file is fine on a newer machine. The disk is quiet and the heat is mild.
avoid: Do not buy a memory stick from the name printed on the old one without checking what the machine accepts. The wrong stick will not be seen.
bench: The counter reads what is fitted and what the board allows. A quote names the stick before it is ordered. Memory does not repair a failing disk.
detail: If the machine is also clicking or losing files, say so. Adding memory on top of a dying disk does not bring the files back.
scene: a laptop memory module held above an open memory slot

title: A Battery That Dies Before Lunch
label: Battery
lead: It leaves the charger full and is nearly empty by noon, on work that used to last the day. Age, a swollen cell, and a hungry program are different.
signs: The percentage jumps from 40 to 10. The time left estimate is a fiction. It dies while the brick is plugged in.
avoid: Do not trust a calibration video as the repair. A worn pack does not regain its old capacity by being drained on purpose.
bench: The pack is measured. A worn pack is replaced with one the machine accepts. If it dies on the charger as well, the adapter and the charging circuit are part of the look.
detail: Say whether it dies only on battery or also while plugged in. Those are two quotes.
scene: a worn laptop battery beside a charger brick on a bench

title: A Battery Icon That Never Moves While Plugged In
label: Battery
lead: The plug is in, the brick is warm, and the percentage stays where it was. The pack may be the cause, or the machine may not be charging it.
signs: The light on the brick is on and the laptop light is not. It runs from the plug and the battery stays at zero. It charges for a minute and stops.
avoid: Do not leave it buried in a sofa while you wait for the number to move.
bench: Adapter, jack, and pack are tested as three pieces. A pack that will not take current is replaced. A jack that only charges at an angle is a different part.
detail: Bring the charger you actually use. A test with a stranger's brick hides the fault that lives in yours.
scene: a laptop battery icon area blurred, with a charger connected on a desk

title: A Charger Brick That Is Too Hot to Hold
label: Repairs
lead: The brick has always been warm. Hot enough to pull your hand away, or a smell from the brick, is past warm.
signs: The cable at the brick is brown or stiff. The laptop charges and the brick smells. A cloth was left over the brick.
avoid: Do not cover the brick, and do not keep using one that smells. Unplug it.
bench: The brick is tested for voltage and for heat under a normal load. A failed brick is replaced with one of the right rating. The laptop is checked only if it still misbehaves on a known-good brick.
detail: A laptop that will not charge is not automatically a bad battery when the brick is the part that smells. Start with the brick you brought.
scene: a laptop charger brick and cable on a desk, no brand logos

title: Using Another Laptop's Charger
label: Repairs
lead: The plug fitted, so it was used. The tip can fit and still be the wrong voltage. That is how charging circuits die.
signs: The laptop is hotter than usual on this brick. It charges slowly or not at all. The old brick was lost and this one came from a different model.
avoid: Do not keep testing bricks until one feels like it works. A wrong one can work for a day and fail the board.
bench: The rating on the brick is compared with what the machine wants. If the board already fails on the correct brick, that damage is named before any new brick is sold.
detail: Bring both bricks if you have them. The look takes minutes and saves a wrong purchase.
scene: two different laptop charger tips side by side on a bench, logos hidden

title: A Power Socket That Wiggles in the Laptop Case
label: Repairs
lead: The metal socket moves when the plug does. Charge cuts in and out. Left alone, the movement cracks the board around the socket.
signs: The socket spins a little. The case around it is cracked. Charge returns only when the plug is pushed in hard.
avoid: Do not glue the plug into the socket. The next step is a harder break.
bench: The jack is resoldered or replaced, and the board around it is checked for lifted pads. The quote says if the pads are already gone, because that is a larger repair.
detail: A wiggling socket is a mechanical fault. Software will not tighten it. The earlier it is brought in, the smaller the job usually is.
scene: a loose round power jack inside an opened laptop chassis

title: A Cracked Laptop Screen, and What Still Works Behind It
label: Screen
lead: The glass is starred or spidered. Some cracked panels still show a picture. Some are black. The crack and the picture are both part of the note you bring.
signs: You can still read through the crack. Ink-like blotches are spreading. The picture is gone and the crack is the reason.
avoid: Do not press the crack to see if it spreads, and do not put tape across the leak if the panel is already bleeding.
bench: A new panel is fitted when the panel is what failed. The cable is checked because a crack and a cable fault can arrive together after a drop. The model decides the panel. No price is printed here.
detail: A blotch that grows after the crack is liquid crystal leaving the glass. Leave the lid as still as you can on the way in.
scene: a cracked laptop screen with a visible fracture, no brand logo

title: Coloured Lines Across a Laptop Screen
label: Screen
lead: A line, or a set of lines, stays in the same place. It can be the panel, or the cable, or a graphics fault. Movement of the lid is the clue.
signs: The lines change when the lid moves. The lines stay put at every angle. An external screen has no lines.
avoid: Do not flex the lid to chase the lines away. You will finish the cable.
bench: If an external screen is clean and the lines follow the lid, the cable or the panel is the job. If the external screen shows the same lines, the board side is looked at before a panel is ordered.
detail: Bring it with the lines as they are. A photo of the lines helps, but the lid test on the bench is what names the part.
scene: a laptop display with vertical coloured bands, no readable text

title: A Screen That Stays Dim at Full Brightness
label: Screen
lead: The slider is at the top and the glass is still dull, or it is bright only in a dark room. The backlight is failing, or a setting is stuck.
signs: A torch shows a clear picture that the backlight will not light. It was dim after a fall. An external screen is normally bright.
avoid: Do not take the bezel off to look at the lamps. The bezel clips break.
bench: A stuck setting is separated from a weak backlight. A backlight or panel job is quoted only when the picture itself is present and the light is not.
detail: If a torch at an angle lets you read the desktop, say so at the counter. That sentence points at the light, not at a dead board.
scene: a very dim laptop screen in a bright room, content unreadable

title: A Touchscreen That Taps When Nobody Is Touching It
label: Screen
lead: The pointer clicks on its own. Windows open and close. A touchscreen with a crack, or with liquid under the glass, often does this.
signs: It happens after a crack. It happens when the room is humid. A USB mouse is calm and the glass is not.
avoid: Do not keep tapping to reset it, and do not spray cleaner into the edges.
bench: The digitiser and the panel are identified for that model. Some are one part. The quote names that part. A board fault is not the first guess when the chaos is only touch.
detail: If the picture is fine and only the touch is wild, say that. It stops the counter from treating it as a graphics fault.
scene: a finger above a laptop touchscreen that is opening windows on its own

title: Keyboard Lights That No Longer Come On
label: Keyboard
lead: The keys still type and the backlight stays dark, or the light flickers with the lid. It can be the lamp sheet, the cable, or a key that no longer toggles it.
signs: The toggle key does nothing. The light works only at one lid angle. The keys are fine in daylight and useless in the dark.
avoid: Do not peel the keyboard to find the light sheet. That sheet tears.
bench: The toggle is tested, then the cable, then the sheet. A dark backlight with a good keyboard is not always a new keyboard. The quote names the piece.
detail: A light that follows the lid angle belongs with the cable through the hinge, the same path as a flickering screen.
scene: a laptop keyboard in a dark room with only a few keys faintly lit

title: A Laptop Key That Came Off
label: Keyboard
lead: The cap is in your hand, or it is lost. Under it, a white hinge may still be there, or it may be broken. Those are different repairs.
signs: The cap clicks back and falls off again. The hinge underneath is in two pieces. Several caps from the same row are loose.
avoid: Do not glue the cap to the keyboard. The key will not travel, and the glue spreads.
bench: A cap and hinge can be refitted when the switch underneath still works. A torn membrane or a missing switch is a keyboard replacement. The counter looks before it glues anything. It will not glue.
detail: Bring the cap if you still have it. The right cap for that position is not always in a drawer.
scene: a detached laptop keycap and its plastic scissor hinge on a blue mat

title: The Touchpad Clicks While You Type
label: Repairs
lead: The cursor jumps into another paragraph while your palms rest. Sometimes that is a setting. Sometimes the pad is too sensitive because the palm rest has warped.
signs: It started after the battery area rose. It happens only when you type hard. A mouse is steady and the pad is not.
avoid: Do not tape the pad down as a permanent fix. Find out whether the case is swollen underneath.
bench: A raised pack is checked first, because a swollen battery pushes the pad. If the case is flat, the pad sensitivity and the pad itself are the rest of the look.
detail: If the trackpad is physically higher than it was, read the swollen-battery notes and switch the machine off. Do not keep typing on it.
scene: hands typing on a laptop with palms close to the touchpad

title: Speakers That Crackle When the Volume Is Up
label: Repairs
lead: Quiet speech is fine. Music or a call at normal volume breaks into crackle. A torn speaker and a failing codec both do this, at different moments.
signs: It crackles only on the left. Headphones are clean at the same volume. It crackles on headphones too.
avoid: Do not push the volume to the top to clear it.
bench: A speaker that crackles alone is replaced. Crackle in the headphones as well moves the look to the board side. The quote follows that test.
detail: Say which side crackles, and whether headphones do it too. That is the whole first question.
scene: a tiny round laptop speaker on a blue mat

title: A Microphone Meetings Cannot Hear
label: Repairs
lead: The call connects and the other person hears nothing, or they hear the room and not your voice. The mic may be muted in the app, blocked, or dead.
signs: A headset mic works and the built-in mic does not. Neither works. The mic array sits behind a clogged hole in the bezel.
avoid: Do not poke the mic hole with a pin.
bench: The setting, the privacy switch, and the mic hardware are separated. A dead mic on the board or in the bezel is quoted as a part. A mute you did not know about is not a paid part.
detail: Try a known headset before you walk in, and say what happened. It shortens the counter conversation.
scene: a laptop bezel microphone hole shown in close detail

title: A Webcam That Shows a Black Picture
label: Repairs
lead: The meeting opens and the picture is black, or the camera is not in the list. A shutter, a driver, and a dead module are three different ends.
signs: A physical shutter is slid across. The camera vanished after an update. The picture is black and the lamp beside the lens never lights.
avoid: Do not peel the bezel to reseat the camera. The bezel is easy to scar.
bench: Shutter and privacy settings are checked first. A module that never lights is replaced when that model allows it as a separate part. Some are glued into the lid and the quote says so.
detail: Look for a slider next to the lens before you book the repair. A closed shutter is not a fault.
scene: a laptop webcam lens with a small privacy slider, no brand logo

title: A Bluetooth Mouse That Will Not Stay Connected
label: Repairs
lead: The mouse works, then the pointer freezes, then it works again. The laptop card, the mouse, and a crowded radio can each do this.
signs: A cable mouse is steady. The Bluetooth mouse is not. It fails only near the router or a USB drive.
avoid: Do not buy a second mouse until the laptop side has been tried with one known-good device.
bench: The wireless card and its drivers are checked when every Bluetooth device fails. A mouse that fails alone, while headphones stay connected, is the mouse.
detail: Bring the mouse you use. A test with the shop's mouse only tells half the story.
scene: a wireless mouse next to a laptop on a wooden desk

title: Why a Laptop Overheats on a Bed or a Cushion
label: Repairs
lead: The intake is on the bottom. A bed closes it. The fan then runs hard and the chip slows down or the machine switches off.
signs: It is fine on a table and hopeless on a quilt. The bottom is hotter than the keyboard. It shuts down only in the evening on the sofa.
avoid: Do not put it on a pillow and then book a fan replacement for a problem the pillow is causing.
bench: If it still overheats on a hard table, the fan and the sink are the job. If it only overheats on soft surfaces, the counter will say so and you may not need a part.
detail: Try one evening on a table before you carry it in. Tell the counter what changed.
scene: a laptop sitting on a bed with the vents blocked by a blanket

title: Monsoon Moisture Inside a Laptop
label: Repairs
lead: The laptop came in from the rain, or it sat in a damp room, and now it will not start or the keyboard types on its own.
signs: It was fine before the rain. The bag was wet. Keys press themselves the next morning.
avoid: Do not put it in rice, and do not power it on to check. Rice dust is a second fault.
bench: It is dried properly and checked for corrosion before it is powered. A keyboard or a board is named only if drying is not enough. The quote comes after that look.
detail: The useful delivery is a laptop that has been switched off since it got wet. Bring the charger separately.
scene: a closed laptop and a damp bag on a bench after rain

title: A Laptop That Will Not Start After a Power Cut
label: Repairs
lead: The lights went out while it was charging. Now it is silent, or it starts and complains about the disk.
signs: There is no light and no fan. It starts and asks for a disk check. The charger was in the wall when the power returned with a surge.
avoid: Do not keep holding the power button down for a minute at a time. Note what, if anything, still lights.
bench: Adapter and board are checked when there is no sign of life. A disk that was writing when the power died is checked before Windows is reinstalled. The files are mentioned first.
detail: A surge can kill a charger and leave the laptop fine, or the other way around. Bring the charger that was plugged in.
scene: a laptop and charger unplugged after a power cut, room lights dim

title: A Student Laptop That Has to Last Through Exams
label: The shop
lead: Exams are close and the laptop is slow, hot, or dying at the desk. The useful repair is the one that finishes before the paper, not a long wish list.
signs: It stalls when many notes are open. The battery will not last a paper. The hinge is loose and the lid is risky to carry.
avoid: Do not book three repairs and hope they all land the night before. Name the one fault that would stop the exam.
bench: The counter will say what can be done in the time you have, and what should wait. A quote is still given before paid work. No promise is made that every machine is a same-day job.
detail: Walk it in during the open hours and say the exam date. Monday to Saturday the counter is open 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM, and Sunday 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM.
scene: a student backpack and a closed laptop on a wooden desk

title: A Gaming Laptop Whose Fan Roars During Play
label: Repairs
lead: A gaming machine runs warm. A gaming machine that throttles, stutters, and roars on a game it used to play smoothly has a heat path that is no longer clear.
signs: The frame rate falls after ten minutes. The fan note has changed to a rattle. It is fine in the menu and hopeless in the game.
avoid: Do not undervolt from a random guide as a substitute for a clogged sink.
bench: The sink, the fan, and the paste are the usual job. A dying fan bearing is a new fan. The quote names which of those the bench found.
detail: Dust in a thick gaming sink does not blow out of the rear vent with a short puff. It is a strip-down.
scene: a thick gaming laptop open on a bench with the fans running

title: A Laptop That Misbehaves Only When It Is Docked
label: Repairs
lead: On its own the laptop is fine. On the office dock the screens flicker, the network drops, or it will not charge. The dock, the cable, or the USB-C port may be the cause.
signs: Two screens work and the third flickers. It charges from the dock and not from its own brick, or the reverse. Undocked, every fault disappears.
avoid: Do not replace the laptop for a fault that vanishes when the dock is removed.
bench: The port on the laptop is tested with a known-good charger and screen. If those work, the dock is the side to replace, and that may not be a laptop repair at all. The counter will say so.
detail: Bring the dock if you can, or describe which faults vanish when you unplug it. That description is the diagnosis.
scene: a laptop connected to a dock and an external monitor on an office desk

title: An Apple Laptop That Says the Battery Needs Service
label: Battery
lead: The machine itself reports that the battery needs service, or the percentage has become a guess. This counter replaces packs. It is not an Apple store and it does not claim to be.
signs: The service message is on screen. The lid does not quite close. Run time has collapsed over a few months.
avoid: Do not ignore a swelling pack because the message can be dismissed. Swelling is a stop-using sign.
bench: The pack is inspected and, when it is the fault, replaced with a pack the machine can use. The quote is given before the work. No official Apple warranty is implied here.
detail: If the pack is swollen, switch it off and carry it rather than posting it. Say that it is swollen when you call 099724 47766.
scene: a thin metal laptop with the battery service area out of focus

title: A Laptop That Says the Adapter Is Not Recognised
label: Repairs
lead: A message says the adapter is unknown, or the charger wattage is wrong, and the machine slows down or refuses to charge.
signs: The original brick was replaced with a cheaper one. The message is new and the brick is the old one. It charges and still shows the warning.
avoid: Do not tape over the centre pin if your plug has one. That pin is how some machines identify the brick.
bench: The brick and the sense pin are tested. A brick that no longer identifies itself is replaced. A jack that has lost the sense contact is a board-side job and is quoted separately.
detail: Bring the brick that produces the message. A different brick hides the test.
scene: a laptop charger plugged in with a small warning dialog blurred

title: A Laptop Whose Caps Lock Blinks and Nothing Starts
label: Repairs
lead: You press power. There is no picture. A light on the keyboard blinks in a pattern. That pattern is a hardware code, not a Windows error.
signs: The blinks repeat. There is no fan, or the fan starts and stops with the blinks. It began after a memory upgrade.
avoid: Do not keep reseating parts you just installed without noting what changed.
bench: The pattern is read against that maker's codes as a hint, then the part it points at is tested. A hint is not a quote. The failed part is confirmed on the bench.
detail: If you added memory or a disk the same day the blinks began, say so. Bring the old part if you still have it.
scene: a dark laptop keyboard with the caps lock light glowing

title: A Laptop Lid That Has Become Loose on One Side
label: Screen
lead: One hinge still holds. The other has torn out of the lid or the base. The screen may still work. The structure does not.
signs: The lid twists as it opens. A crack is growing from the hinge into the bezel. The screen flickers only on the loose side.
avoid: Do not carry it open. Do not open it from the loose corner.
bench: Hinge, lid cover, and base posts are quoted as the pieces that are actually broken. A panel is added only if the picture has failed too.
detail: A loose lid and a cracked panel after one drop can be one event and two parts. The counter names both before work starts.
scene: a laptop lid twisted slightly because one hinge has failed

title: A Laptop That Slows Down When Several Tabs Are Open
label: Repairs
lead: Two tabs are fine. Twenty tabs, and the fan starts and the scrolling stutters. Memory, heat, and a crowded browser are the three usual reasons.
signs: It recovers when you close the browser. It does not recover until it cools. The disk light is busy the whole time.
avoid: Do not assume it needs a new laptop because a heavy browser page made it stall.
bench: The bench separates a short memory, a hot chip, and a disk that cannot keep up. The quote matches the one it finds. You may be told to close tabs and not to buy a part.
detail: Note whether a minute of rest brings the speed back. If rest fixes it, talk about heat. If rest does nothing, talk about memory or the disk.
scene: a laptop with many browser tabs, the tab titles blurred

title: A Laptop Fan That Rattles When It Speeds Up
label: Repairs
lead: A tick or a rattle appears as the fan climbs, and it may vanish at full speed. A blade is touching, or the bearing is oval.
signs: The rattle is new after a drop. It comes and goes. The machine is hotter than before the noise began.
avoid: Do not push a pin into the vent to stop the tick.
bench: The fan is removed and spun. A bent blade or a dead bearing is a new fan. The sink is cleaned while it is open if it is packed with dust, and that is said in the quote.
detail: A rattle plus new heat means the fan is no longer moving enough air. Do not wait for the shutdowns to start.
scene: a laptop cooling fan held in a hand above a blue mat

title: A Password Screen That Appears Before Windows
label: Repairs
lead: A password is demanded as soon as you press power, before any Windows logo. That is a firmware password. It is not the Windows password, and it is not something this page can print.
signs: You never set it. It appeared after a shop you no longer trust. You set it years ago and the word is gone.
avoid: Do not pay a random tool that claims a master password for every brand. Many of those are lies, and some make the lock harder.
bench: The counter will tell you honestly whether that model can be reset and what you lose if it can. On some machines the honest answer is that the board stays locked. That is said before any money is taken.
detail: Bring proof the laptop is yours. A locked firmware is not an invitation to bypass someone else's machine.
scene: a laptop firmware password box on a black screen, text unreadable

title: A Laptop That Restarts Before the Desktop Appears
label: Repairs
lead: The logo shows, the dots spin, and the machine restarts. It never offers a password. Software, disk, and heat can each loop like that.
signs: It loops three times and then offers a repair screen. It loops only when warm. It started after a failed update.
avoid: Do not hold the power button through ten loops. You are only wearing the disk.
bench: Startup repair, disk health, and heat are checked in that spirit. A clean install is offered when the system is the fault and you have agreed about the files.
detail: If it reaches the desktop when you wait an hour for it to cool, say so. That is a heat job, not a new Windows.
scene: a laptop stuck on a spinning startup indicator, no readable logo

title: Windows Automatic Repair That Never Finishes
label: Repairs
lead: A screen says it is preparing automatic repair, and an hour later it is still there, or it restarts into the same screen.
signs: It began after the power was lost. It began after an update. You can still reach a blue menu with options.
avoid: Do not choose reset this PC until you know your files are copied. Reset is a wipe of the apps and often of the files.
bench: The disk is checked before any reset is recommended. If the disk is dying, repair screens will not finish because they cannot read. The quote then becomes a disk job, with the files discussed first.
detail: A repair that never finishes is often the disk, not a stubborn Windows. Mention clicks or missing files if you have noticed them.
scene: a laptop showing an automatic repair screen, words out of focus

title: A Message That Says No Boot Device
label: Storage
lead: The firmware cannot find a disk to start from. The disk may be loose, dead, or no longer marked as the one to boot.
signs: It appeared after a bump. It appeared after an internal clean you tried yourself. A USB stick is plugged in and the message changes.
avoid: Do not change a pile of firmware settings you do not know. Write down nothing you cannot undo.
bench: The drive is reseated and tested. A drive that is absent is replaced only after you have said whether the files on it matter. A drive that is present and not selected is a setting, not a new part.
detail: Remove USB sticks and memory cards before you call, and try once more. If the message remains, bring it in with the charger.
scene: a laptop firmware message about a missing boot device, text blurred

title: Only the Browser Is Slow
label: Repairs
lead: Documents are fine. The browser spins. That is often extensions, a full disk, or one bad site, not a dying motherboard.
signs: One site is slow and others are not. Every site is slow and a document is quick. It became slow after a new extension.
avoid: Do not reinstall Windows for a tired browser.
bench: The counter looks at whether the rest of the machine is healthy. A cleanup of the browser and startup items is a small job. If the disk is also failing, that is the real quote and the browser was only the symptom you noticed.
detail: Try another browser once before you walk in. If the second browser is fast, say so.
scene: a laptop browser window loading slowly, page text blurred

title: A Laptop That Freezes on Large Spreadsheets
label: Repairs
lead: A short sheet is fine. A large one turns the cursor to a wheel and the fan starts. Memory and heat are the usual reasons. A failing disk is the other.
signs: It only freezes on one file. Every large file does it. The file lives on a network or a USB disk.
avoid: Do not keep force-closing the program and reopening the same huge file ten times. Save a copy somewhere else first if you can.
bench: Memory fitted, disk health, and temperature under that load are checked. The quote matches the weak piece. A new machine is not the opening offer.
detail: Say how large the file is in ordinary words, and whether a small file in the same program is fine.
scene: a laptop open to a spreadsheet with the cursor busy, numbers blurred

title: A Laptop That Stopped Scanning After an Update
label: Repairs
lead: The printer still prints and the scanner does not, and an update landed the day it changed. Drivers and the USB path are the likely jobs.
signs: The scanner is not in the list. It scans from another laptop. The USB port used for it is the loose one.
avoid: Do not download a driver from a site that is not the scanner maker.
bench: The port is tested, then the driver is put back cleanly if the port is sound. A dead USB controller is named only when other USB devices have died too.
detail: Try the scanner on another computer if you can, and try another port. Tell the counter which of those worked.
scene: a flatbed scanner cable next to a laptop on a desk

title: A Laptop That Says the Printer Is Offline
label: Repairs
lead: The printer is on, and the laptop says it is offline. The queue, the network, and a stuck job are more common than a dead printer.
signs: It prints from a phone and not from the laptop. One document is stuck at the head of the queue. It failed after the Wi-Fi name changed.
avoid: Do not install the printer three times. Remove the stuck queue first.
bench: This counter is a laptop bench, not a printer workshop. If the laptop's network or USB side is the fault, that is the job. If the printer fails from every device, you will be told to take the printer elsewhere.
detail: Check whether a phone on the same Wi-Fi can print. That answer decides whose machine is the fault.
scene: a small office printer beside a laptop, no brand names visible

title: An External Monitor That Flickers When Driven by the Laptop
label: Screen
lead: The laptop glass is steady and the external screen flickers, or the other way around. Cable, port, and refresh rate are the first three checks.
signs: A different cable is steady. The flicker follows a cheap adapter. The laptop screen flickers too.
avoid: Do not buy a new monitor until the cable and the port have been tried.
bench: If the laptop glass is also flickering, the job may be the laptop panel or cable, and the external flicker is a clue rather than a second fault. The counter looks at both.
detail: Bring the cable you use. A perfect shop cable can hide a tired cable that is the whole problem at home.
scene: a laptop connected to an external monitor that looks slightly unstable

title: Sound That Stays in the Laptop When a Television Is Connected
label: Repairs
lead: The picture is on the television and the sound is still in the laptop, or there is no sound at all. The output device, not the speakers, is often the switch.
signs: Picture is correct and sound is not. It worked on another television. An adapter sits between the laptop and the television.
avoid: Do not assume the laptop speakers have died because a television is silent.
bench: The output path is checked. An adapter that carries picture and not sound is identified so you do not pay for a speaker repair you do not need. A dead HDMI port is a different quote.
detail: Try the television's own apps. If those have sound, the television is fine and the link from the laptop is the question.
scene: a laptop HDMI lead running toward a television, brands hidden

title: A USB-C Screen the Laptop Will Not Drive
label: Screen
lead: The USB-C port charges, or it does not, and the screen on that port stays black. Not every USB-C port on a laptop can drive a screen.
signs: One port charges and the other does video. A USB-C hub shows USB devices and no picture. The same screen works on a different laptop.
avoid: Do not buy a second hub until you know the port is meant to do video.
bench: The port is identified. If that model has no video on the port you are using, you will be told, and you will not be sold a board for a limit of the design. A failed port that used to do video is a repair and is quoted.
detail: Bring the hub or the cable. Say whether this port ever showed a picture.
scene: a USB-C cable plugged into the side of a slim laptop

title: A Laptop That Will Not Charge From USB-C
label: Repairs
lead: The USB-C charger used to fill the battery. Now the light never comes, or it comes only on one side of the laptop.
signs: A different charger works. No charger works in that port. The port is loose.
avoid: Do not force a damaged plug. Bent shells crack the port.
bench: The port, the charger rating, and the pack are separated. A worn port can be replaced on many models. A charger that is below the wattage the machine wants is not a port fault.
detail: Bring the USB-C charger you use, not a phone charger, unless the phone charger is the one that failed.
scene: a USB-C charger plugged into a slim laptop on a wooden desk

title: A Trackpad That Has Risen in the Middle
label: Battery
lead: The pad is proud of the palm rest, or it clicks on one side only. The usual reason is a battery underneath that has swollen.
signs: The lid will not close. The pad rocks. You can see a gap along the front edge.
avoid: Do not screw the pad down tighter. You will be clamping a swelling cell.
bench: The pack is inspected first. If it is swollen, it is replaced and the pad is checked afterwards. A pad that was damaged by the swelling is named in the same conversation, before work.
detail: Treat a risen pad as a battery fault until the bench says otherwise. Switch the machine off and do not charge it overnight.
scene: a laptop palm rest with the trackpad slightly raised

title: A Missing Screw and a Loose Laptop Corner
label: Repairs
lead: A corner lifts, a cover ticks, and a screw is gone. Sometimes that is only a screw. Sometimes the boss it threaded into has torn out.
signs: The cover flaps. You still have the screw. The screw spins and never tightens.
avoid: Do not use a longer screw from a hardware shop. Too long a screw can reach the board.
bench: The correct screw and the boss are checked. A torn boss may need the cover replaced or the post repaired. The quote says which.
detail: Bring any screws that fell out, in a small bag. The right length matters.
scene: tiny laptop screws in a tray beside an open bottom cover

title: A Bottom Cover That Will Not Clip Shut
label: Repairs
lead: The base cover sits proud, or a clip is broken, after a battery change or a drop. An open gap lets the next drop do more damage.
signs: One clip is visibly gone. The cover was forced. A cable is trapped in the gap.
avoid: Do not tape the cover as a long-term fix, and do not trap a ribbon under it.
bench: The clipped cover is refitted properly. A broken clip or a warped cover is replaced when it will not hold. Any cable that was pinched is checked before the cover goes back.
detail: If you opened it yourself and a ribbon is bunched in the gap, stop and bring it. Forcing the cover will cut that ribbon.
scene: a laptop bottom cover slightly ajar on a repair bench

title: What to Say Before an Old Disk Is Replaced
label: Storage
lead: A new SSD makes the laptop quick. It does not, by itself, contain your old files. The files are a separate decision, made before the old disk leaves the bay.
signs: You need the photos. You only need a fast empty machine. You do not know whether the old disk still reads.
avoid: Do not assume a new disk includes a copy. Ask.
bench: The counter asks whether the files matter, then whether the old disk can still be read. A copy is attempted only when you ask and the disk allows it. A disk that will not read is not promised back.
detail: Say the word files before the cover comes off. That is the whole point of this note.
scene: an old laptop hard disk next to a new SSD on a blue mat

title: Copying Files Off a Disk That Already Clicks
label: Storage
lead: The disk clicks and you still need a folder off it. Every extra power-on can be the last one that reads.
signs: Some folders still open. The click is getting louder. You have been restarting it all week to copy a little more.
avoid: Do not keep mining it at home. Do not run a long disk check that hammers a dying drive.
bench: The bench powers it as few times as it can and copies what still reads, if you have asked for that and accepted that not everything may come. A new disk is a separate line on the quote.
detail: Write down the folder names that matter most. The first copy should be those, not the whole drive.
scene: a hard disk connected for a careful file copy on a repair bench

title: When a Clone Is the Right Job, and When It Is Not
label: Storage
lead: A clone copies the old disk onto a new one, faults included. That is right when the old disk is healthy and you want the same system. It is wrong when the old system is the thing that is broken.
signs: The old disk is slow but the files and the programs are fine. The old system is full of pop-ups. The old disk already clicks.
avoid: Do not clone a clicking disk and expect a healthy machine. You may clone the failure, or the copy may not finish.
bench: The counter recommends a clone when the disk is sound and a clean install when the system is not. A clicking source is a file-copy attempt, not a clone, and it is described that way.
detail: Say whether you need your programs exactly as they are, or only your documents. The job follows that answer.
scene: two drives side by side ready for a copy, on a blue mat

title: A Clean Windows Install, and What You Lose
label: Repairs
lead: A clean install is a new system on the disk. Programs, and often the files, are not in that new system unless they were copied first.
signs: The desktop no longer arrives. You want a fresh start and you have a copy of your documents. You do not have a copy and you hope the install keeps them.
avoid: Do not agree to a clean install in a hurry at the counter if you have not talked about the files.
bench: The install is done when you have agreed what is kept and what goes. A product key or account sign-in may be needed afterwards. That is said before the work, not after.
detail: Bring the Microsoft account details if the machine uses one. A local account can be a new one you choose.
scene: a laptop on a Windows setup screen, all text blurred

title: No Wi-Fi After Windows Is Installed
label: Repairs
lead: A fresh system often has no driver for the wireless card. The card is usually fine. The driver was simply not in the clean Windows.
signs: Wi-Fi is missing and Ethernet or a phone tether works. The wireless device is an unknown device. It failed only after the install, not before.
avoid: Do not conclude the card died during the install.
bench: The driver for that card is put back when the card is sound. If the card is absent in a hardware look, then it is a part, and that is a different quote.
detail: This is a common end to a clean install. Mention it when you collect the machine if the network list is empty.
scene: a laptop network list that is empty, text unreadable

title: Windows Activation After a Main Board Change
label: Repairs
lead: A new or replaced board can make Windows ask to be activated again. The digital licence lived with the old board or with your account.
signs: It says activate after a board repair. You are signed into the Microsoft account that was on the machine. You never had an account on it.
avoid: Do not buy a random cheap key from a banner.
bench: The counter explains that activation is a licence question, not a soldering question. Where the licence can be moved, you will be told what to sign in with. Where it cannot, that is said plainly.
detail: Know which email was on the laptop before the board failed. Bring that, not a guess.
scene: a Windows activation watermark area, text deliberately blurred

title: A Laptop That Forgets the Time Every Morning
label: Repairs
lead: Every cold start, the clock is wrong, and sometimes the machine asks for the date before it will boot. The small coin cell that keeps that clock is often flat.
signs: The time is wrong only after it has been unplugged overnight. Certificates and websites complain. It asks for the date before Windows.
avoid: Do not ignore it for months. A wrong clock breaks sign-in to some sites and can confuse updates.
bench: The coin cell is tested and replaced when it is flat. On some models it is an easy part. On others it is under the board, and the quote says so before the work.
detail: Set the time once and unplug it overnight. If it is wrong again, the cell is the likely job. Tell the counter that test.
scene: a small coin cell battery next to an opened laptop

title: When a Keyboard Must Be Replaced, Not Cleaned
label: Keyboard
lead: Sticky keys from dust can be cleaned. Keys that died after a spill, or a membrane that has torn, are a replacement. The look takes a minute and saves the wrong job.
signs: One key is sticky and the rest are fine. A whole row died after tea. Letters type on their own.
avoid: Do not wash the keyboard under a tap.
bench: The bench says clean or replace. A replacement on many laptops is the whole keyboard assembly, sometimes with the top case. That is in the quote before anyone orders it.
detail: A single sticky key with a crumb under it is not a new keyboard. A row of dead keys after a spill usually is.
scene: a laptop keyboard half lifted from the palm rest

title: Tea or Coffee in the Keyboard
label: Keyboard
lead: Sugar and milk are worse than plain water. They stay, they corrode, and they gum the keys. Speed matters more than a wipe with a tissue.
signs: The drink was sweet. Keys in that area are already dead. The laptop is still on.
avoid: Switch it off. Unplug the charger. Do not turn it on to check the keys.
bench: The pack comes off, the area is cleaned, and corrosion is looked for. A keyboard is replaced when the contacts are gone. A board is named only if the drink reached it. The quote follows what is seen, not the size of the cup.
detail: The sooner it is off and in the shop, the less far the liquid travels. Call 099724 47766 and say it was tea or coffee, not just water.
scene: a small spill of tea across a laptop keyboard

title: A Fault That Looks Like a Bad Panel and Is the Cable
label: Screen
lead: Lines, flicker, or a black screen that changes when the lid moves are often the cable through the hinge. A new panel would not have been the fix.
signs: It is perfect at one angle. A slight bend of the lid brings the picture back. The problem grew as the hinge loosened.
avoid: Do not buy a panel from a website on the strength of a flicker.
bench: The cable is tested by movement and, when needed, by substitution. A panel is ordered only when the cable is not the cause. You hear that choice before the part is bought.
detail: Tell the counter the picture changes with the lid. That one fact steers the job away from the wrong part.
scene: a thin laptop display cable running through a hinge

title: A Screen Bezel That Has Come Away
label: Screen
lead: The plastic frame around the glass is loose, cracked, or missing a clip. The picture may still be perfect. The bezel still matters, because it holds the lid together.
signs: A corner sticks out. The webcam area is loose. It broke when the hinge was already weak.
avoid: Do not superglue the bezel to the glass. The next opening will tear the panel.
bench: The bezel is refitted or replaced, and the hinge is checked because a loose bezel and a loose hinge often travel together. Glue is not the repair used here.
detail: If the picture has also failed, say so. The bezel job and the panel job are listed separately.
scene: a laptop screen bezel pulled slightly away from the glass

title: Broken Plastic Around the Laptop Hinge
label: Repairs
lead: The metal hinge may still be strong while the plastic it lived in has crumbled. The lid then splits even though the picture is fine.
signs: White stress marks spread from the hinge. A piece of plastic is already in the bag. The lid no longer opens evenly.
avoid: Do not keep opening it from the weak side to check whether it has got worse.
bench: The cover that holds the hinge is replaced when the posts are gone. A hinge is replaced when the metal is the broken part. The quote names which of those the bench is looking at.
detail: Bring the broken pieces. They show which cover failed.
scene: cracked plastic around a laptop hinge, pieces on a blue mat

title: A Battery Percentage That Jumps
label: Battery
lead: It says 50, then 15, then it shuts down, then it says 40 on the charger. The gauge and the pack no longer agree, or the pack is worn out.
signs: The jump is sudden. It happens at the same percentage every day. It also dies while plugged in.
avoid: Do not spend a week on calibration if it also shuts down under load.
bench: The pack is measured under load. A pack that collapses is replaced. A gauge that is merely confused, on a healthy pack, is a smaller job and is described that way.
detail: If it only misreports and never dies, say that. If it dies in the middle of work, say that instead. They are different.
scene: a laptop battery percentage that looks inconsistent, digits blurred

title: Charging a Laptop Only to 80 Percent on Purpose
label: Battery
lead: Some machines stop at 80 percent because a setting asked them to, to save the pack. That is not a fault. A pack that cannot pass 80 and then dies at lunch is a fault.
signs: It always stops at the same number and runs a normal day. It stops at that number and is empty an hour later. You turned on a care mode and forgot.
avoid: Do not replace a pack for a limit you switched on.
bench: The setting is checked first. If no limit is set and the pack still will not charge or hold, the pack is tested and quoted.
detail: Look for a battery care or conservation switch before you book. If you find one, try a day with it off and see what the number does.
scene: a laptop charging on a desk, screen content out of focus

title: Leaving a Laptop Plugged In Every Night
label: Battery
lead: Modern packs stop calling for current when they are full. Heat is the bigger overnight problem: a laptop charging under a pillow, or a brick covered by a cloth.
signs: The brick is too hot in the morning. The pack has started to swell. Nothing has changed except the heat of the room.
avoid: Do not bury a charging laptop in bedding. Do not cover the brick.
bench: If the pack is already swollen or the run time has collapsed, that is a pack inspection, not a lecture. The counter looks at the pack and quotes only if it needs to be replaced.
detail: Heat plus swelling is a reason to switch it off and bring it in. Heat alone, with a flat lid and a normal day of battery, may not be a repair at all.
scene: a laptop charging overnight on a hard desk, brick uncovered

title: Carrying a Hot Laptop in a Closed Bag
label: Repairs
lead: The machine is closed and slid into a bag while the fan is still trying to cool it. The heat has nowhere to go, and hinges and disks do not enjoy that.
signs: It is very hot when you take it out. It will not wake until it has sat open. The bag is thick and the vent was against the padding.
avoid: Do not shut the lid and bag it at the end of a heavy job. Give it a minute on the table.
bench: If it now shuts down, throttles, or the disk has started to click since this became a habit, the bench looks at heat damage and the disk. The quote follows what failed, not the bag.
detail: The habit is yours to change. The repair, if a part has already suffered, is the counter's.
scene: a closed laptop being placed into a padded bag

title: What the Counter Needs to Know After You Travel With the Laptop
label: The shop
lead: Bags are dropped, trays are bumped, and power in another place is not always kind. A fault that began on a trip has a story that helps.
signs: It died after a fall from the tray. The charger no longer matches because you bought one there. It was rained on between the gate and the cab.
avoid: Do not hide the drop. The story saves the wrong diagnosis.
bench: Impact, liquid, and a strange charger are three different openings. Tell the truth about which one happened. The look and the quote follow that.
detail: Walk the machine in. This counter does not collect from the airport or from a flat. The address is Ganesh Complex, above the TVS showroom, Hosur Road, opposite Infosys.
scene: a closed laptop in a travel sleeve on a bench

title: What a Repair Quote Should Name Before Work Starts
label: The shop
lead: A fair quote names the fault, the part if a part is needed, and the work of fitting it. A single number with no nouns is not a quote you can judge.
signs: You were told a total and not a fault. Two faults were found and only one was mentioned. You want the words before you agree.
avoid: Do not agree to a number you cannot repeat back as a job.
bench: At this counter the fault is named before any paid work. If a second fault appears once the machine is open, it is said before that extra work starts. No price list is printed on this site. The number is for the machine in front of the technician.
detail: Ask what the job is, in ordinary words. If the answer is only a price, ask again.
scene: a notebook and pencil beside an open laptop on a wooden counter

title: What to Bring With the Laptop to the Counter
label: The shop
lead: The laptop, the charger you actually use, and a sentence about the fault. That is the useful set. A box of every cable you own is not required.
signs: The fault involves charging, and the brick is at home. The fault involves a dock, and the dock is at the office. You need a password the technician will hit.
avoid: Do not bring it without the charger if the complaint is that it will not charge.
bench: The counter can test with a shop brick, and will say when it did. Your brick is still the better test when the brick is the suspect. Passwords are asked only if the fault is behind the sign-in, and you can stay for that part.
detail: Walk in during open hours. Monday to Saturday, 10:00 AM to 8:00 PM. Sunday, 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM. Call 099724 47766 if you want to know whether to come today.
scene: a laptop and its charger brick placed together on a counter

title: What Can Be Finished the Same Day, and What Cannot
label: The shop
lead: A part that is on the shelf and a fault that is obvious can be the same day. A panel that has to be ordered for your exact model cannot be invented by the evening.
signs: You are leaving the city tonight. The part is common. The part is a particular panel.
avoid: Do not promise yourself a same-day panel for an uncommon model. Ask.
bench: The counter says whether the part is in hand. If it is not, the quote includes the wait. No one pretends a courier part is already on the bench.
detail: Phone first if the timing matters. Describe the model and the fault. The answer is honest, including when the answer is not today.
scene: a repair bench with a few laptop parts laid out, not a stockroom

title: The Six Parts on the Shop Board
label: The shop
lead: The board lists a charger, a battery, a hard disk, RAM, a keyboard, and a motherboard. Those are the families of part this counter fits. The one for your machine is chosen after the look, not from the board alone.
signs: You want whatever is drawn on the board. You do not yet know which of the six is the fault. Two of them might be, and you want them separated.
avoid: Do not point at the board and ask for one of each.
bench: The fault is named, then the part that matches that fault is quoted. A motherboard is not the opening offer for a dead charger. A charger is not the offer for a clicking disk.
detail: The same six are the daily work. Screens and heat are part of the bench as well. The services page lists the work in one place.
scene: a simple repair shop board area with laptop parts, no readable brand text

title: A Second Fault Found After the Laptop Is Open
label: The shop
lead: The job you agreed was a fan clean. Under the cover, the battery is swollen, or a port is cracked. That second fault is not done in silence.
signs: You came for one thing. The technician has found another. You want to know before anyone continues.
avoid: Do not feel you must agree to the second job on the spot. Hear it, then decide.
bench: This counter stops and tells you. The second job has its own words and its own agreement. You can take the machine after the first job only, if that is still safe. A swollen pack is described as a safety matter, not as a surprise extra.
detail: Ask to be told before any extra paid work. That is already how this bench is meant to run.
scene: an open laptop on a bench with two separate parts set to the side

title: Only One Laptop Speaker Is Silent
label: Repairs
lead: Music comes from one side only. The other speaker is quiet or dead. A balance setting, a loose plug, and a failed speaker are three different ends.
signs: The balance slider is already centred. Headphones play in both ears. The quiet side is the one nearest a drop or a spill.
avoid: Do not push the volume to the top to wake the quiet side. Do not open the bezel to look.
bench: Balance is checked, then each speaker. A dead speaker is replaced when that model uses a separate part. If both sides fail inside the headphones as well, the look moves off the speakers and the quote says so.
detail: Tell the counter which side is quiet, and whether headphones are even. That sentence decides whether a speaker is ordered at all.
scene: one small laptop speaker beside an open chassis on a blue mat

title: Collecting the Same Laptop You Brought In
label: The shop
lead: You should leave with the machine you carried in, repaired, not with a swap you did not agree to. Know a mark on it: a scratch, a sticker, the serial if you wrote it down.
signs: You are collecting after a repair. Someone else is collecting for you. You want to see the fault is gone before you go.
avoid: Do not collect in a rush without switching it on.
bench: Switch it on at the counter. Look at the fault you came for. If a part was replaced, ask what was replaced. The machine you take is the one you brought, unless you agreed otherwise, and you will not be asked to agree to a swap in the ordinary job.
detail: If a friend will collect it, tell them the fault to check. The counter is at Ganesh Complex, above the TVS showroom, opposite Infosys, Electronic City.
scene: a closed laptop being handed across a wooden shop counter
